rationale: PINS #841 round 7: Groovy 3's IDENTITY operators `===` and `!==`, which the grammar had no production for at all. The load-bearing assertion is forbidErrors, for the same reason as the other #841 grammar pins: recovery did not stop at the operator, it swallowed the ENCLOSING CLASS, so a missing-edge assertion would not have detected the defect. Legality is not assumed — the two corpus files that use these operators (ColumnConfigSpec.groovy and HibernateConnectionSourceSettingsSpec.groovy) are both in the parse oracle's ACCEPTED set, i.e. real Groovy 3.0.24 parses them while our grammar rejected them (validation/m59/results/g841-groovy-oracle.json). Corpus consequence at the rebuilt wasm (grails-core @ a83f8748, whole tracked corpus, production parseFile pipeline): 272 -> 269 error files, 3 fixed, 0 regressed, crashes 0, pipeline mismatches 0; ERROR nodes 4.0% -> 3.9%. NOTE: per reviews/m59-841-assert-comma-separator.md 7h the corpus A/B was run FIRST for this change and the fixture lane second, because the previous grammar attempt passed 61/61 fixtures and 51/51 mutants while breaking 1,480 corpus files. authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun is false: the expectation was authored from live emission via script/m14/tmp/g841-fixture-dump.ts.
